author: Wehrle, Günther, et al.

Major Step 2 describes the sample selection based on RNA quality as well as the preparation for sectioning of bone and multi-tissue musculoskeletal samples from mice. The steps are based on the Visium FFPE tissue preparation guide available at: https://www.10xgenomics.com/support/spatial-gene-expression-ffpe/documentation/steps/tissue-prep/visium-spatial-gene-expression-for-ffpe-tissue-preparation-guide.9.Place FFPE block on 4°C plate or on metal block in freezer (<5 min).10.Set-up microtome and insert blade.11.Clamp FFPE block in microtome.12.Align complete surface of FFPE block to the blade (90°).13.Trim FFPE block until all tissues on block are exposed/representative of tissues later to be placed on the Visium slide.14.Cut a section of 10 μm (without water flow turned on) and immediately place the rolled-up section with autoclaved tweezers into a pre-cooled autoclaved Eppendorf tube.15.Repeat step 14 3x, to pool 4 sections of 10 μm per FFPE tissue block in one Eppendorf tube.16.Immediately proceed to RNA isolation or intermediately store the Eppendorf tube with the pooled sections at −80°C – Pause point (days – weeks).17.Isolate RNA using the RNeasy FFPE kit (QIAGEN) – Pause point.18.Immediately proceed to DV200 measurements or intermediately store the RNA at −80°C – Pause point (days – weeks).19.Determine the DV200 using a TapeStation and select samples meeting the requirements of the specific spatial transcriptomics platform (e.g., DV 200 ≥ 50% for Visium FFPE spatial transcriptomics) – Pause point (days – weeks).

steps.title: Prepare workspace and reagents
steps.instruction: Set up a sterile, cold work area and prepare all reagents and equipment before animal work.

substeps.instruction: Wear gloves.
Fill Falcon tubes with ~12 mL of 10 % neutral‑buffered Formalin, place tubes on ice and add Formalin.
Wipe all table surfaces with 70 % ethanol.
Place and fix anesthesia mask on Table 1.
Place heating mat on Table 1, cover with drape or paper towel.
Arrange shaver, large scissors, tweezers (± lancets) on Table 1.
Place a sterile Folio‑drape on Table 2 and tape its edges to the table.
Fill a plastic box with ice so the ice surface is ~1 cm below the rim; flatten the ice.
Put the ice‑filled box in the centre of the Folio‑drape without touching other areas.
Place one closed Petri dish on the ice.
Place autoclaved surgical instruments (scissors, tweezers, scalpel blade) next to the box on the Folio‑drape in a sterile manner.
Prefill the anesthesia induction box with 3 % isoflurane.

steps.title: Harvest femur tissue from mouse
steps.instruction: Anesthetize, euthanize, and dissect the right femur (with optional muscle) while keeping the procedure under 10 min to preserve RNA.

substeps.instruction: Place mouse in induction box until asleep (slow respiration).
Optional: wear two pairs of sterile gloves and record body weight.
Transfer mouse to the table and maintain inhalation anesthesia via mask.
Optional: collect blood via cardiac puncture or facial vein.
Turn isoflurane to maximum.
Shave right and left femur and the distal back of the mouse.
Euthanize by cervical dislocation or decapitation and confirm complete tissue disconnection.
Place mouse on a second ice‑cooled Petri dish.
Make a circumferential skin incision around the right femur with scissors.
Incise the upper hind‑limb muscles toward the hip joint.
Ex‑articulate the hip joint by manual rotation.
Remove the right hind limb and place it on the lid of a Petri dish.
Remove the outer pair of gloves.
Hold the tibia with tweezers (cranial part facing down) on the Petri dish.
Use a scalpel blade 11 or 15 to disconnect tibia from femur at the knee joint.
Transfer the femur ± surrounding muscle into pre‑cooled 10 % neutral‑buffered Formalin.
Note: muscle can be removed as desired; femur and quadriceps may stay together; external fixator may be removed now or kept until embedding.
Complete steps h–o within 10 min.

steps.title: Fix, decalcify and embed tissue
steps.instruction: Fix the harvested tissue, decalcify, dehydrate, clear and embed in paraffin following the detailed temperature‑controlled program.

substeps.instruction: Fix tissue in 10 % neutral‑buffered Formalin for 16–24 h (up to 24 h) at 4 °C.
Decalcify in pre‑chilled 12.5 % EDTA (pH 7.5) for 10 days at 4 °C; exchange EDTA solution every 3 days.
Transfer tissue with tweezers into a histology cassette and incubate sequentially in 30 %, 50 % and 70 % ethanol for 1 h each.
Optional: separate bone and muscle with scissors and place into separate cassettes.
Load cassettes into a tissue processor with the following program:
1) 70 % ethanol at 37 °C for 1 h,
2) 70 % ethanol at 37 °C for 1 h,
3) 100 % ethanol at 37 °C for 30 min,
4) 100 % ethanol at 37 °C for 30 min,
5) 100 % ethanol at 37 °C for 1 h,
6) Isopropanol at 40 °C for 1 h,
7) Isopropanol at 45 °C for 1 h,
8) Paraffin at 62 °C for 4.5 h.
Remove samples from the processor and proceed to paraffin embedding.
For muscle, cut cross‑sections; for bone, align the femur axis with the embedding mold.

If an external fixator is present, hold it with tweezers while embedding, fill paraffin until the bone is covered (do not let paraffin dry), carefully remove the pins, then completely fill the mold with paraffin and place the cassette on top.
Place the embedding mold on a 4 °C plate for 3–7 h.
Remove the FFPE block from the mold and store at 4 °C in a refrigerator (pause point: days to years).

steps.title: Select block and cut sections for RNA QC
steps.instruction: Trim the FFPE block, cut four 10 µm sections, pool them, and assess RNA quality before proceeding to Visium.

substeps.instruction: Place the FFPE block on a 4 °C plate or metal block in a freezer for <5 min.
Set up the microtome and insert a fresh blade.
Clamp the FFPE block in the microtome.
Align the block surface to the blade at 90°.
Trim the block until all tissue of interest is exposed.
Cut a 10 µm section (water flow off), roll it up with autoclaved tweezers, and transfer into a pre‑cooled autoclaved Eppendorf tube.
Repeat the previous step three more times to pool four 10 µm sections per block in one tube.
Proceed immediately to RNA isolation or store the tube at –80 °C (pause point).
Isolate RNA using the QIAGEN RNeasy FFPE kit.
Proceed immediately to DV200 measurement or store RNA at –80 °C (pause point).
Measure DV200 on a TapeStation; retain samples with DV200 ≥ 50 % for Visium FFPE.

steps.title: Section and place tissue on Visium slide
steps.instruction: Section the paraffin block, score if needed, and mount 5 µm sections onto the capture areas of a Visium FFPE slide.

substeps.instruction: Wipe the microtome, water bath and all surfaces with RNase‑Away.
Thoroughly flush the water bath with Milli‑Q water.
Set up the microtome and a 42 °C water bath using Milli‑Q water.
Place a lamp beside the water bath for bright illumination.

If the tissue exceeds the capture area, score it with a scalpel blade 11 or 15 (room temperature ~20 °C) or a microtome blade (room temperature ~20 °C). Ensure paraffin remains within the scored region and keep one bone end intact.
Submerge the scored paraffin block in an ice‑cold Milli‑Q water bath (sample surface down) for 5–10 min.
Clamp the block in the microtome and re‑align the surface with a MX35 blade (Epredia).
Trim until intact 10 µm sections are obtained.
Remove paraffin debris with a dedicated brush (do not reuse for other tasks).
Connect a water slide to the water bath and place sections onto a Superfrost slide with a brush.
Inspect the section under a microscope for integrity.
Cut one 10 µm section followed immediately by a 5 µm section (the latter will be used on the Visium slide).
Allow sections to float in the water bath, then turn off water flow to facilitate handling.
Remove any paraffin or tissue outside the scored area with two fine brushes.
Let the section float until wrinkles disappear.
Visually confirm integrity, especially at bone‑muscle interfaces.
Mark the capture areas on the back of the Visium slide with a water‑resistant marker.
Using a fine brush, place the 5 µm section onto each capture area, ensuring all tissue lies within the capture area (paraffin may extend beyond).
Repeat for three additional sections/capture areas.

steps.title: Deparaffinize, stain and image slides
steps.instruction: Follow the 10× Visium FFPE protocol (CG000409 Rev D) for deparaffinization, H&E staining, imaging and decrosslinking, handling slides gently to avoid tissue loss.

substeps.instruction: Perform all steps exactly as described in Visium protocol CG000409 Rev D.
Use sterile tweezers when handling Visium slides to protect RNA quality.
Critical: transfer the slide slowly from one solution to the next to prevent tissue detachment.

steps.title: Probe hybridization, library prep and sequencing
steps.instruction: Execute the Visium FFPE workflow (CG000407 Rev E) for probe hybridization, ligation, library construction and sequencing, taking care with wash steps.

substeps.instruction: Perform all steps exactly as described in Visium protocol CG000407 Rev E, including all quality‑control checkpoints.
Critical: add wash buffers slowly to the side of the gasket to avoid tissue detachment.

steps.title: Analyze Visium spatial transcriptomics data
steps.instruction: Process raw sequencing data through Space Ranger, perform downstream analysis with Seurat/Scanpy, and visualize results together with histology.

substeps.instruction: Install required software and dependencies; download mouse reference genome, probe‑set reference file and slide layout GPR file as indicated in the software requirements.
Run Space Ranger’s mkfastq to demultiplex Illumina BCL files into FASTQ files.
Align FASTQ reads to the mouse reference genome with Space Ranger count, generating spatial feature matrices and filtering barcodes.
Analyze spot‑level expression using Seurat (R) or Scanpy (Python).
Conduct quality control: filter spots by total counts and number of expressed genes; exclude spots with high mitochondrial or ribosomal read fractions.
Normalize and scale data; identify highly variable genes with SC‑Transform.
Perform dimensionality reduction; use elbow plots to select the appropriate number of principal components.
Cluster spots using a shared‑nearest‑neighbor (SNN) modularity algorithm.
Visualize clusters with UMAP and overlay the UMAP clusters onto the histology image.

Carry out downstream analyses such as marker‑gene identification, cell‑type annotation, spatial segmentation, trajectory inference, cell‑cell interaction, detection of spatially variable genes, differential expression and pathway enrichment.
Annotate tissue regions with QuPath and extract spot coordinates and barcodes using the 10× Loupe Browser.

description: Bone adaptation and healing are spatially and mechanically controlled processes3 involving crosstalk of multiple tissues.4 Preservation of the spatial context represents a transformative advancement in cellular profiling technologies (e.g., RNA sequencing) with the potential to supplant established histology-based methods, such as in situ hybridization, immunohistochemistry and dissociated single-cell techniques. Whereas spatial transcriptomics analyses have successfully been applied in many research areas,5 its use in bone has been limited due to the calcified nature of the samples often associated with tissue detachment from slides. Recently, spatial transcriptomics approaches have been described for cryo-embedded skeletal samples from P0 calvaria and during digit regeneration in mice.4,6,7 To allow for broader application of spatial transcriptomics in musculoskeletal research, we have now established a protocol for FFPE calcified tissue samples from mice. Here we describe a detailed protocol that permits the use of spatial transcriptomics (Visium, 10× Genomics) in bone and multi-tissue musculoskeletal FFPE samples from mice. The protocol below describes the specific steps for samples from an externally-stabilized femur defect model in mice. However, we have also used this protocol for bone samples (vertebra, intact femur), muscle samples (m. quadriceps femoris) and multi-tissue samples (intact femur with adjacent muscle). The protocol is structured into seven steps ranging from tissue harvesting and preparation to the final analyses of the sequencing data. The complete protocol takes ca. 18 days for mouse femora with adjacent muscle; of this time >50% is required for mineralized tissue decalcification. Potential pause points are indicated in the detailed description of the procedure.
